newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian parliament debates anti-pyramid law.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parliament debates anti-pyramid law.

text.p: Albania's parliament on Wednesday began debating a draft law to regulate the nation's remaining high-yield investment schemes and prevent a re-run of the pyramid scheme scandal that toppled the last government.

The bill, worked out in cooperation with experts from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, authorises the new Socialist-led government to appoint foreign or local firms to administer the high-interest schemes.
These schemes escaped being outlawed earlier this year when the government banned so-called pyramids.
"It gives the administrators of these companies full power over their activitities and assets," said a document accompanying the draft law.

Albania's new coalition government said it was keen to pass the law later on Wednesday ahead of an international donors' conference in Rome that starts on Thursday. Albania is seeking international aid to rebuild its shattered economy.

At the start of the year, the collapse of fraudulent pyramid schemes, which offered rates of interest similar to those offered by the surviving investment schemes, sparked street protests which degenerated into widespread anarchy.
A financial expert said the draft law did not cover the collapsed schemes. That was now a matter for the courts.
The government is keen to appoint a foreign company to audit the remaining high interest savings schemes in order to lend credibility to the process and avoid accusations of bias.
It is hoping international organisations will finance the operation.
A small group of deputies was concerned that the law should not violate the property rights of the audited firms.
Four companies with creditors across Albania are either paying back only small sums of money to depositors or have frozen payments altogether, citing security concerns.
One company has admitted owing money to 80,000 creditors.
